technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Cloud Data Flow for streaming pipeline modules and shell integration.
Use Spring Shell library for adding Hadoop command support in the shell.
Leverage Spring Batch and Spring Cloud Task for composed job orchestration and repository options.
Implement message binding via Spring Cloud Stream's expression-based routing and binder abstractions.
Use Spring Kafka and Spring Hadoop for Kafka source and HDFS sink modules respectively.
Migrate JDBC and Kafka modules from Spring XD to Spring Cloud Stream repos while preserving APIs and compatibility.
Adopt JUnit 5 and Mockito for isolated shell command unit testing as per the linked document.
Use standard Maven/Gradle multi-module project structure for all modules.
assumptions: The developer has deep familiarity with Spring ecosystem (Spring Boot, Cloud Stream, Batch, Shell, Data Flow).
All user stories are to be implemented in the same increment; no dependencies between them that would require sequential ordering.
Effort estimates include analysis, coding, unit/integration testing, basic documentation, and code review.
Existing test infrastructure and CI pipelines are in place; no additional setup overhead beyond typical development.
The linked document for U5 provides sufficient detail to implement isolated shell command tests without additional exploration.
Migration tasks (U7, U8) involve moving existing code with minimal refactoring, but require verification and adaptation to new repo structure.
No major architectural changes are needed; designs follow existing patterns in Spring Cloud Stream and Data Flow.
Each user story is sized as a moderate complexity feature, not requiring extensive research or third-party library integration beyond what is already standard.

activities.activity_description: Develop a new HDFS sink module for Spring Cloud Data Flow to write streaming pipeline data to Hadoop HDFS. Includes module creation, Spring Hadoop integration, configuration, unit/integration tests, and registration in module registry.

Implement Spring Shell commands for Hadoop filesystem operations (e.g., ls, put, get) in the Spring Cloud Data Flow shell. Includes command classes, parameter handling, integration with Hadoop client, and unit tests.

activities.activity_name: Explore and implement repository options for composed jobs
activities.activity_description: Analyze and implement a repository (e.g., in-memory, JDBC) for storing composed job definitions. Includes design, coding of repository interfaces and implementations, integration with Spring Batch, and tests.

Implement functionality to orchestrate multiple jobs into a single workflow (composed job). Includes job flow definition, execution logic, error handling, and integration tests with Spring Cloud Task/Batch.

activities.activity_name: Add test coverage for shell commands in isolation
activities.activity_description: Develop unit tests for shell commands that mock external dependencies (e.g., Hadoop) to allow isolated testing without end-to-end deployments. Follow the linked document's guidelines.

activities.activity_name: Support XD-like message binding via expressions
activities.activity_description: Add support for Spring XD-style expression-based message binding in Spring Cloud Stream modules. Implement a mechanism to bind message properties to module inputs using SpEL expressions, including configuration, binder integration, and tests.

activities.activity_name: Move JDBC module from XD to s-c-s repo
activities.activity_description: Migrate the existing JDBC sink module from Spring XD repository to the Spring Cloud Stream repo. Adapt code to new project structure, ensure compatibility with Spring Cloud Stream APIs, and verify functionality with tests.

activities.activity_name: Move Kafka module from XD to s-c-s repo
activities.activity_description: Migrate the existing Kafka source module from Spring XD repository to the Spring Cloud Stream repo. Adapt code, update dependencies to Spring Kafka, verify source functionality, and add integration tests.
